en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Maiden Mādrī, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Garden of Anāthapiṇḍada. At that time...
Ānanda went out with his alms bowl to beg for food.
Having finished eating, Ānanda was walking along the edge of the water when he saw a woman carrying water away from the bank. Ānanda asked the woman for some water, and she gave it to him.
The woman then followed Ānanda, watching the place where he stayed.
The girl returned and told her mother; her mother’s name was Mātaṅgī. The girl threw herself on the ground at home and wept.
Her mother asked her, "Why are you weeping so sorrowfully?"
The girl said, "Mother, if you wish to give me in marriage, do not give me to another.
By the water's edge, I saw a śramaṇa begging for water from me; I asked him what his name was."
"Her name is Ānanda.
I shall marry only when I obtain Ānanda; if I do not obtain him, I will not marry.
Her mother went out to inquire about Ānanda, and she learned that Ānanda was serving the Buddha.
The mother, having learned this, returned and told her daughter:
"Ānanda serves the Buddha’s path and is unwilling to be your husband.
The daughter wept, refusing to eat or drink, and said:
"The mother knows the way of sorcery.
When the mother went out, she invited Ānanda to return for a meal, and the daughter was greatly delighted.
The mother said to Ānanda:
"I wish to give my daughter to you as a wife. Ānanda said,
"I observe the precepts and do not maintain a wife."
She spoke again, saying,
"If my daughter does not obtain you as her husband, she will take her own life.
Ānanda said:
"My teacher, the Buddha, does not permit sexual intercourse with women.
The mother went in and told her daughter:
"Ānanda is unwilling to be your husband; he says that one who possesses the Way of the Sūtras may not keep a wife."
The daughter replied to her mother while weeping,
"Where is the path of the Mother?
Her mother said:
"In all the paths of the world, there is none that can surpass the path of the Buddha or the path of the Arhat.
Māndārī again said, "Just close the doors for me so that no one may escape; at dusk, you shall naturally become my husband."
The mother closed the door and bound Ānanda with sorcery.
When the time of *pradoṣa* arrived, the mother prepared a mat for her daughter to lie upon; the daughter was overjoyed and adorned herself.

Ānanda refused to go forward to the place where he was to lie down. His mother caused a fire to break out on the ground in the middle of the courtyard; she went forward, pulled Ānanda by his robe, and said to him:
"If you will not become my daughter's husband, I shall throw you into the fire."
Ānanda felt self-disparaging, thinking that though he had become a śramaṇa under the Buddha, today he was instead trapped within this place and unable to escape.
The Buddha, exercising his supernormal power, knew Ānanda’s thoughts with his own mind.
Ānanda returned to where the Buddha was and said to him:
"Yesterday, while going on my almsround, I saw a woman by the water's edge and asked her for some water."

I returned to the place where the Buddha was; on the following day, a woman named Māndhātṛ invited me to take a meal at her home. As soon as I went out, she seized me, wishing to give her daughter to me to be my wife.
I said, "I uphold the Buddha's precepts and am not permitted to keep a wife.
When the woman saw that Ānanda had escaped and departed, she wept and wailed at home.
The mother said:
"As for those who serve the Buddha, my path cannot surpass theirs.
Did I not tell you this from the beginning?"
The girl did not stop weeping and continued to think of Ānanda.
On the following day, she went out herself to seek Ānanda; seeing him again begging for food, she followed behind him, gazing at his feet and gazing at his face.
Ānanda felt ashamed and withdrew, but the woman continued to follow him without ceasing.
Ānanda returned to the Buddha’s presence, yet the woman remained guarding the gate; when Ānanda would not come out, the woman wept and departed.
Ānanda went before the Buddha and said,
"The daughter of Mātaṅga has followed me again today.
The Buddha sent someone to call for the daughter of Mātaṅga.
Seeing her, the Buddha asked,
"What are you seeking as you pursue Ānanda?
The woman replied:
“I have heard that Ānanda has no wife, and I, too, have no husband; I wish to become Ānanda’s wife.
The Buddha said to the woman:
“The śramaṇa Ānanda is hairless, whereas you have hair. Are you able to shave off your own hair?”
"I shall have Ānanda serve as your husband.
The woman said,
"I can shave my hair."
The Buddha said,
"Return and inform your mother that you have shaved your hair and are coming.
The girl returned to her mother's place and said:
"The mother could not bring Ānanda to me," [the Buddha] said, "and the Buddha declared:
'Shave off your hair and come; I shall have Ānanda act as your husband.
The mother said:
“Child! I gave birth to you and have protected your hair; why do you wish to become the wife of a śramaṇa?
In this kingdom there are great and wealthy families; I myself can marry you to one of them.”
The girl said,
"In birth and death, I shall become Ānanda’s wife.
Her mother said:
"Why do you bring shame upon my lineage?
The woman replied, "If you,
Mother, love me, you should follow what my heart desires."
The mother wept as she took up the razor and shaved her daughter's hair.
The daughter returned to where the Buddha was and said,
"I have already shaved my hair."
The Buddha asked,
"What is it that you love about Ānanda?
The woman replied:
"I love Ānanda’s eyes; I love Ānanda’s nose; I love Ānanda’s mouth; I love Ānanda’s ears; I love Ānanda’s voice; I love Ānanda’s gait."

The Buddha said: "In the eyes there is only tears; in the nose there is only mucus; in the mouth there is only saliva; in the ears there is only wax; and within the body there are only the foul and impure places of excrement and urine."

Those who have husbands and wives inevitably encounter impurities; from these impurities comes a child, and with the child comes death; with death comes weeping. In this regard, what benefit is there in this body?
The woman immediately reflected upon the impurities within her own body; she then rectified her mind and attained the path of Arhatship.
Knowing that she had attained Arhatship, the Buddha addressed her, saying:
"Arise and go to Ānanda."
The woman immediately felt ashamed and lowered her head; kneeling long before the Buddha, she said:
"It was truly out of ignorance that I followed Ānanda!
Now my mind has been opened, like a lamp lit in the darkness."
It is like a person riding in a boat who, when the boat breaks, clings to the shore;
like a blind person who has found support;
or like an elderly person walking with the aid of a staff.
"Now the Buddha has bestowed the Way upon me, causing my mind to open in this way.
All the bhikṣus together asked the Buddha:
"This woman’s mother practiced sorcery; by what causes and conditions did this woman attain the path of an arhat?"
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"Do you wish to hear and know about this woman?
The bhikṣus replied:
"We shall receive your instruction," they said.
The Buddha said:

"In previous lives, for five hundred lifetimes, this woman Māndārī was Ānanda’s wife. Throughout those five hundred lifetimes, they always respected and honored one another, and were mutually fond of and affectionate toward each other. They attained the Way together within my sūtras and precepts; now, when husband and wife meet, it is like meeting brothers."
"If this is so, what use is it not to practice the Buddha-way?
When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, all the bhikṣus who heard it were filled with joy.
This concludes the *Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Woman Mādrī*.
